q: What is the maximum period within which a small station has to be inspected by an Accounts Officer?
e: The correct answer is 6 months. . Small stations earn and handle relatively less traffic cash, so the Accounts Officer inspects them at the longest prescribed maximum interval. Larger stations are inspected more frequently because the volume of cash and the risk of irregularity are higher. This graded periodicity is part of the inspection regime under Chapter 23 of the Accounts Code. Related exam fact: the detailed day-to-day inspection of stations is done by Travelling Inspectors of Accounts (TIAs), whose work the Accounts Officer test-checks.

q: Which para of Chapter 23 of Accounts Code prescribes Intensive Check over collection of Tickets?
e: The correct answer is 3306. Option B is the correct para. Chapter 23 of the Accounts Code, which governs inspection of station accounts, prescribes an intensive check over the collection of tickets to detect malpractices such as re-sale of collected tickets. During this check the TIA examines ticket tubes, closing numbers and the Daily Trains Cash Book. Related exam fact: Chapter 23 also provides for the Accounts Officer to test-check the work of the inspectors.

q: Which of the statements given from a to d is not correct?

options.A: TIA can inspect a station as per schedule identified by the Traffic Accounts office.
options.B: TIA can conduct a system check of fares and distance in UTS
options.C: TIA cannot check records of Private Freight Terminal
options.D: TIA cannot take records for inspection outside station premise in case of a fraud on his own.

e: The correct answer is TIA cannot check records of Private Freight Terminal. Option C is the statement that is not correct. The other three statements correctly describe the duties and powers of inspecting officials under the station-inspection regime of Chapter 23 of the Accounts Code, so only this one contradicts the codal position. In the exam, test every statement against the codal provisions before choosing. Related exam fact: the TIA is expressly empowered to instruct station staff on the preparation of returns and the manner of keeping books.

q: How would a TIA access records which are stored on UTS/PRS/ FOIS?

options.B: They will access the records through the station master’s ID.
options.C: A unique ID and Password is to be provided for them for the required period.
options.D: TIA themselves have an ID on the portals.

e: A unique ID and Password is to be provided for them for the required period. — that is the right answer. . Records held in the computerized systems — UTS, PRS and FOIS — are accessed by the TIA through system-generated reports and authorized data extracts, not through physical books. The inspector relies on MIS reports and fare dumps made available via the Traffic Accounts Office for such checks. Related exam fact: a systems audit of FOIS, UTS and PMS is separately provided for under para 3313 of the codal provisions.

q: A TIA goes to station and finds that the manner in which the books and accounts are being kept at the station are not correct. What should he/she do ? clarify

options.A: Note down the same and put it in the report
options.C: Note it down as well as the proper method of maintaining books of accounts and records by instructing the station staff.
options.D: Come back to HQ and report to the Accounts Officer

e: Note it down as well as the proper method of maintaining books of accounts and records by instructing the station staff. — that is the right answer. . When the TIA finds that the books and accounts at a station are not being kept correctly, he instructs the station staff on the correct procedure and reports the matter to the Accounts Officer. Inspectors are expressly empowered to give instructions on the preparation of returns and the manner of keeping books and accounts. Related exam fact: the Station Master must give the TIA free access to all records during inspection.

q: Checking the stock position of Ticket Rolls,in relation to requirement and comment on position of overstock or understock is in case of ______
e: Option B (UTS/PRS) is the correct choice. . Checking the physical stock of ticket rolls against the station's requirement, and commenting on overstock or understock, is the prescribed check for UTS ticket rolls. Overstock locks up working capital in idle ticket stock, while understock risks ticket shortages at the counter. Related exam fact: the TIA also checks the arrangement of tickets in tubes and agrees the dates and closing numbers with the tube summary and the Daily Trains Cash Book.

q: What is the check on part of TIA’s for Cash Bags? Choose the closest from among the following.
e: Signature of Guard — that is the right answer. . Cash bags in which stations remit their earnings must be properly sealed, correctly entered in the remittance records and promptly dispatched, and the TIA checks exactly these points. This ensures station cash reaches the bank or cash office intact and without delay. Related exam fact: verification of cash and instruments immediately on arrival is the opening step of every station inspection.

q: Recovery of Demurrage and Wharfage has to be checked ____

options.C: No checks required as TA office checks it on its own

e: Option A (Only in manual 1 only) is the correct choice. . Recovery of demurrage — charges for detention of wagons beyond free time — and wharfage — charges for occupying goods-shed space beyond free time — has to be checked by the inspecting officials. These are valuable goods earnings that stations sometimes fail to collect or under-collect. Related exam fact: wharfage and demurrage returns are also test-checked periodically in the Traffic Accounts Office.

options.C: Accounts officers and Commercial authorities in unison
options.D: Reserve force of Inspectors of Traffic Accounts

Being unannounced, they are the most effective way to catch cash shortages, ticket irregularities and defective record-keeping red-handed. Inspection is the on-the-spot verification of cash, stores, tickets and records to ensure rules are followed and leakages caught early. options.B: With officers from the TA office
options.D: Surprise inspections should be carried out alone

q: What does systems audit of FOIS / UTS / PMS imply as per codal provisions , Para 3313?

options.A: Review of stock in the system

e: Option C (Review of concessional schemes) is the correct choice. . Para 3313 of the codal provisions provides for systems audit of the computerized systems FOIS, UTS and PMS. A systems audit examines system controls, masters and data integrity rather than manually vouching individual transactions, so that fares, distances and charges generated by the systems can be relied upon. Related exam fact: TIAs access these system records through authorized reports and data extracts during station inspection.

Balance sheets of non-railway locations such as JTBS, YTSK and out agencies are not sent directly to the Traffic Accounts Office; they are routed through the nominated serving station.
